column1: # ZAP baseline accepted risks (plan §18.3).
# Format: <ruleId>
# Anything NOT listed here fails the nightly scan. Every entry states why, and entries are
# reviewed whenever the nightly run changes -- an ignore with no reasoning is how a real
# finding gets buried.
# Non-Storable Content. Flags pages that cannot be cached. Ours are deliberately
# `no-store`: every page is either personalised, an overlay whose URL is a credential, or a
# break page that must never serve a stale total. This rule is the inverse of a finding for
# us -- storable content would be the bug.

column3: Pages are intentionally no-store (per-user, overlay credentials, live totals)

column1: # Modern Web Application. Informational: ZAP noting the app is JS-driven and it therefore
# cannot follow every link by spidering. True, and not a vulnerability. It is why the
# Playwright suite carries the browser-level security assertions instead.

column3: Informational: app is JS-driven by design; browser assertions live in the e2e suite

column1: # Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy missing. COEP `require-corp` exists to enable cross-origin
# isolation (SharedArrayBuffer, precise timers). We use neither, and enabling it would
# break the OBS overlay's ability to be embedded by a browser source without buying
# anything. COOP and CORP -- the two that actually limit what other origins can do to us --
# ARE set. Revisit if we ever need cross-origin isolation.

column3: COEP not set deliberately: no cross-origin isolation needed; COOP and CORP are set

column1: # CSP rule family. Accepted ONLY for `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, which React's style prop
# and Tailwind's injected styles both require; removing it means nonced <style> tags plus
# style-src-attr, whose browser support is uneven enough to risk an unstyled page in Safari.
# Tracked as a known gap in docs/asvs-checklist.md rather than pretended away.
# This rule id also covers wildcard sources, which we do NOT accept -- a ZAP baseline found
# `img-src ... https:` on 2026-09-20 and it was fixed. Because an ignore here would hide a
# regression of that, the narrower property is asserted directly in the browser instead:
# see "carries no wildcard fetch sources" in apps/web/e2e/catalog.spec.ts.

column3: style-src 'unsafe-inline' accepted; wildcards guarded by an e2e assertion instead

column1: # Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens. A heuristic that looks for a hidden token field in a form.
# Ours is submitted by script to the auth API, which checks the Origin header -- verified
# by accident during Phase 2, when a request without an Origin was rejected with 403.
# Session cookies are also SameSite=Lax. A hidden field would add nothing.

column3: CSRF is handled by Origin checks + SameSite=Lax cookies, not by a form token
